facts.statement: Delapparentia is a genus of iguanodont dinosaur that lived in the Early Cretaceous period in Spain.
facts.quote: Delapparentia is a genus of iguanodont dinosaur from the Early Cretaceous period of Galve, Teruel Province, Spain.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Delapparentia was discovered in the spring of 1958 by amateur paleontologist José María Herrero Marzo.
facts.quote: The type specimen, MPT/I.G, was found in the spring of 1958 by amateur palaeontologist José María Herrero Marzo.

facts.statement: Starting from September 25, 1958, the fossil was collected by Professor Dimas Fernández-Galiano with a Dutch team led by Gustav Heinrich Ralph von Koenigswald.
facts.quote: Starting from 25 September 1958, it was collected by Professor Dimas Femández-Galiano, assisted by a Dutch team from the University of Utrecht led by Gustav Heinrich Ralph von Koenigswald.

facts.statement: In 1960, Albert-Félix de Lapparent originally assigned the finds to Iguanodon bernissartensis.
facts.quote: The finds were originally assigned to Iguanodon bernissartensis by Albert-Félix de Lapparent in 1960.

facts.statement: José Ignacio Ruiz-Omeñaca validly named the genus Delapparentia turolensis in a 2011 paper after initially naming it in a 2006 dissertation.
facts.quote: In 2006, José Ignacio Ruiz-Omeñaca named this material as a new taxon, Delapparentia turolensis, in a dissertation; since names published in theses are invalid nomina ex dissertatione, he subsequently validly named it in a 2011 paper.

facts.statement: Delapparentia was a large species estimated to be about 10 meters long and weighing 3.5 tonnes.
facts.quote: Delapparentia was a large species, about 15% longer than Iguanodon bernissartensis. The length has been estimated at 10 m, the weight at 3.5 tonne.

facts.statement: The ilium of Delapparentia measures 78 centimeters in length.
Unique characteristics include posterior dorsal ribs with long, parallel, unfused ends, ossified sternal ribs, and a straight, lateromedially expanded preacetabular process of the ilium.
facts.quote: In the initial description of the genus by Ruiz-Omeñaca, several autapomorphies (unique characteristics) of Delapparentia were established: posterior dorsal ribs with long, parallel and unfused capitula and tubercula, ossified sternal ribs, and a straight and lateromedially expanded preacetabular process of the ilium.

facts.statement: Based on new remains, researchers recognized proportionally high neural spines and related the species to the earlier Barilium from England based on ilium morphology.
facts.quote: On the basis of new remains, Gasca et al. provided a revised diagnosis in which they recognized the proportionally high neural spines, and related it to the earlier Barilium from England on the basis of its ilium morphology.

facts.statement: Ruiz-Omeñaca assigned Delapparentia to the Iguanodontoidea in 2011.
facts.quote: Delapparentia was assigned to the Iguanodontoidea by Ruiz-Omeñaca in 2011.

facts.statement: Some researchers challenge the identification of Delapparentia as a distinct taxon, suggesting it represents an old adult individual of Iguanodon bernissartensis based on neural spine proportions.
facts.quote: The identification of Delapparentia as a distinct taxon has been challenged; Verdú et al. conducted a study of individual variation among specimens of Iguanodon bernissartensis, and found that the neural spine proportions of Delapparentia were not particularly outside the range of variation in I. bernissartensis. They considered Delapparentia to represent an old adult individual of I. bernissartensis.

facts.statement: Delapparentia turolensis lived during the Barremian stage of the Early Cretaceous, approximately 130 million years ago, in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: Delapparentia turolensis es la única especie conocida del género extinto Delapparentia de dinosaurio ornitópodo iguanodóntido que vivió a principios del período Cretácico durante el Barremiense, hace aproximadamente 130 millones de años, en lo que es hoy Europa.

facts.statement: The time range for Delapparentia is estimated from 125.77 to 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: The holotype is a partial adult skeleton lacking a skull, consisting of four cervical vertebrae, twenty-eight neurapophyses, two sacral vertebrae, fourteen caudal vertebrae, rib fragments, chevron fragments, ossified tendons, and a left pubis and ilium.
facts.quote: El holotipo es un esqueleto parcial que carece de cráneo, de un individuo adulto. Consiste de cuatro vértebras cervicales, veintiocho neurapófisis, dos vértebras del sacro, catorce vértebras caudales, fragmentos de las costillas cervicales, dorsales y esternales, fragmentos de cinco cheurones, numerosos tendones osificados y un pubis izquierdo y un iliaco.

facts.statement: Some bones originally misidentified by de Lapparent as belonging to the sauropod Aragosaurus, including an ischium, were later referred to Delapparentia.
facts.quote: Algunos otros huesos, confundidos por de Lapparent como pertenecientes a los del saurópodo Aragosaurus, fueron referidos a Delapparentia, entre ellos un isquión.

facts.statement: The generic name honors Albert Félix de Lapparent, who studied the skeleton and published the first monograph on Spanish dinosaurs titled "Los Dos Dinosaurios de Galve".
facts.quote: El nombre genérico honra a Albert Félix de Lapparent, quien estudió el esqueleto y fue pionero en el estudio de los dinosaurios españoles, publicando la primera monografía sobre el tema en el país: "Los Dos Dinosaurios de Galve".

facts.statement: The specific name is derived from the Latin name of Teruel, Turia.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie se deriva del nombre en latín de Teruel, Turia.

rejected.statement: The fossils were found at the La Maca 3 locality in the Camarillas Formation, dating to the early Barremian stage about 130 to 127 million years ago.
rejected.quote: It was discovered and collected from La Maca 3 locality in the Camarillas Formation of Galve dating to the early Barremian stage (about 130-127 million years ago), and consists of a partial skeleton lacking the skull, of an adult individual.

rejected.quote: It also presents a unique combination of characters, including anterior dorsal ribs with a pneumatic foramen and an ischium that is large in relation to the ilium.
